results.assumptions: Ranked all products across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30) by total units sold, excluding voided orders.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by revenue?

These figures represent total sales across your entire data period, calculated from non-voided orders after applying any line discounts.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross revenue as line-level revenue (unit price * quantity minus line discount) for all non-voided orders across the entire data period.

results.question: Which month had the highest revenue, and how much was it?

results.question: How much revenue came from each sales channel?

results.question: What is the revenue for each store location?

results.question: Compare the average order value for online and in-store orders.

Online customers spent an average of $194.13 across 10,667 orders, compared to $187.49 across 6,673 in-store (POS) orders. These figures exclude any voided orders to keep the comparison accurate.

results.question: Which product type sells the most units?
results.sql: SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, sum(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Accessories sell the most units, with a total of 8,771 units sold. This excludes any voided orders and standardises the product types to lowercase.
results.assumptions: Product types are normalised to lowercase. Voided orders are excluded. Units are summed across all non-voided order lines.

results.question: Which day of the week do we get the most orders, and how many?
results.sql: SELECT to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'Day') AS day_of_week, count(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY to_char(created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney', 'Day'), extract(dow from created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: You get the most orders on Saturdays, with a total of 3,468 orders across the available data. This count excludes any voided orders and is based on Australia/Sydney time.
results.assumptions: Converted order timestamps to Australia/Sydney time, excluded voided orders, and grouped by day of the week over the entire available dataset.

results.question: At the peak hour of the day (Sydney time), how many online orders do we get in total?
results.sql: WITH hourly_orders AS (SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) AS hour_of_day, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE sales_channel = 'online' AND financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY hour_of_day), peak_hour AS (SELECT hour_of_day FROM hourly_orders ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT h.hour_of_day, h.order_count AS total_online_orders FROM hourly_orders h JOIN peak_hour p ON h.hour_of_day = p.hour_of_day;
results.answer: At the peak hour of the day in Sydney time (8 PM), you received a total of 1,232 online orders. This count includes all valid online orders across the entire dataset, excluding any voided ones.
results.assumptions: Analysed all online orders (excluding voided ones) converted to Australia/Sydney time to find the overall peak hour of the day across the entire dataset, and returned the total order count for that hour.

results.question: How much have we given away in discounts in total?

results.question: How much revenue did our dresses bring in?

results.answer: Your dresses brought in a total revenue of $542,989.65 AUD. This figure covers all non-voided orders across the entire data period from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. The calculation is based on net line totals, meaning it accounts for unit prices, quantities sold, and any applied line discounts.
results.assumptions: Filtered products where lower(product_type) = 'dress'. Revenue is calculated as line totals (unit_price * quantity - line_discount) for all non-voided orders across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30).

results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * ol.quantity))::numeric, 2) AS total_gross_profit, ROUND(SUM((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1)::numeric, 2) AS total_ex_gst_revenue, ROUND((SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1 - v.cost * ol.quantity)) / NULLIF(SUM((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1), 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_pct FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL
results.answer: Your overall gross profit margin is 58.32%, based on a total gross profit of $1,584,502.69 and ex-GST revenue of $2,716,823.41. This calculation covers all non-voided orders from October 2025 through September 2026. Please note that any product variants missing cost data were excluded from this margin calculation.
results.assumptions: Calculated overall gross profit margin for all non-voided orders across the entire dataset (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Revenue is converted to ex-GST by dividing by 1.1. Variants with NULL cost are excluded from the margin calculation as per rules.

results.question: What are our top 5 products by gross profit?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, p.product_type, SUM(((ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) / 1.1) - (v.cost * ol.quantity))::numeric(10,2) AS gross_profit FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title, p.product_type ORDER BY gross_profit DESC LIMIT 5;
results.answer: Your top five products by gross profit are the One-Piece Swimsuit at $165,884.48 AUD, Shirt Dress at $130,441.22 AUD, Straw Hat at $108,854.01 AUD, High-Rise Jeans at $104,531.12 AUD, and Wool Coat at $89,912.11 AUD. These figures exclude voided orders and products with missing cost data, and remove GST by dividing revenue by 1.1.
results.assumptions: Calculated gross profit as total line revenue divided by 1.1 (to remove GST) minus total unit cost, excluding variants with NULL cost. Voided orders were excluded.

results.question: What is our net revenue after refunds?

results.answer: Your net revenue after refunds is $3,205,298.79 AUD. This total is calculated by taking all non-voided order revenue and subtracting total refunds. This figure assumes the dataset provided is complete and up to date.
results.assumptions: Net revenue is calculated as total non-voided order revenue minus total refunds across the entire dataset.

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?

results.answer: Your total revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 in July, $282,129.97 in August, and $278,068.87 in September 2026. These figures include all non-voided orders based on their original order date up through September 30, 2026.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql:
WITH eofy_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(total) AS revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count,
    'EOFY Sale' AS period
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < TIMESTAMP '2026-07-06 00:00:00'
),
pre_eofy AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(total) AS revenue,
    COUNT(order_id) AS order_count,
    'Pre-EOFY (Same duration)' AS period
  FROM orders
  WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= TIMESTAMP '2026-06-02 00:00:00'
    AND (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < TIMESTAMP '2026-06-19 00:00:00'
)
SELECT period, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, order_count FROM eofy_sales

SELECT period, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, order_count FROM pre_eofy;
results.answer: Revenue during the EOFY sale was higher, reaching $246,002.91 compared to $186,171.83 in the 17 days right before it. This analysis assumes we are comparing two identical 17-day periods using gross order totals for non-voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, sum(ol.quantity) AS units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines ol ON v.variant_id = ol.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY units_sold ASC LIMIT 3;
results.answer: The three products that have sold the fewest units are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. These figures cover all variants and sales channels across the entire dataset while excluding voided orders.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?

results.answer: A total of 1,640 unique customers have placed 3 or more non-voided orders. This count is based on all available data from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. Please note that guest orders without a customer ID were excluded from this total since they cannot be grouped.
results.assumptions: Counted unique customers with 3 or more non-voided orders across all available data (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Guest orders (customer_id IS NULL) are excluded since they cannot be grouped by customer.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.5 days after an order is placed. This calculation looks at the time between when an order and its corresponding refund were created across all recorded refund events.
results.assumptions: Calculated the average time difference in days between the order creation timestamp and the refund creation timestamp across all refund events.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?

results.answer: You made $944,363.46 in revenue from orders that used a discount. This total only includes non-voided orders where a discount was actually applied.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1;
results.answer: Camel was your top-selling color in the winter of 2026, with a total of 1,050 units sold. This count includes all non-voided orders processed between June 1 and August 31, 2026.
results.assumptions: Winter is defined as June 1 to August 31, 2026, based on Australia/Sydney timezone. Units sold are summed across all non-voided order lines grouped by variant color.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN EXTRACT(ISODOW FROM (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) IN (6, 7) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, ROUND(SUM(total), 2) AS revenue, COUNT(order_id) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue DESC;
results.answer: Weekdays brought in more total revenue than weekends, with weekdays generating $2,147,980.22 across 11,153 orders compared to $1,173,950.49 across 6,187 orders on weekends. This comparison assumes standard five-day weekdays and two-day weekends based on Sydney local time, while excluding any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Compared total revenue and order counts between weekends (Saturday and Sunday) and weekdays (Monday to Friday) using Sydney local time for day-of-week determination, excluding voided orders.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH ranked_products AS (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS product_type, p.title AS product_title, sum(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY lower(p.product_type) ORDER BY sum(ol.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY lower(p.product_type), p.title) SELECT product_type, product_title, total_units_sold FROM ranked_products WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC;
results.answer: The best-selling products by category are the One-Piece Swimsuit in swimwear with 4,043 units, Straw Hat in accessories with 3,619 units, and Linen Wrap Skirt in skirts with 1,804 units. Other top sellers include the Shirt Dress (1,492 units), Ribbed Tank (1,395 units), High-Rise Jeans (1,295 units), Wool Coat (828 units), and Merino Crew Jumper (526 units). These totals include all units sold across non-voided orders with product types grouped in lowercase.
results.assumptions: Best-selling is measured by total units sold across all non-voided orders. Product types are normalized to lowercase to group variants consistently.

results.assumptions: Counting non-voided orders (or all orders since order_lines typically associate with valid orders) where the total sum of quantities across all order lines for that order is greater than 1.
